Youth Gavin Mason prepares to strike in the Tonbridge 1500 metres. Gavin has had a great season over events ranging from 200 to 1500 metres. In the Surrey Schools he ran to 3rd place in the 800 metres with 1:58.0.

Adam Jones was another who would have expected to place a lot higher, so in spite of a brilliant 34th from Matt Hillier, who was really flying over the last section of the race, and an equally impressive 54th from Gavin Mason, the team had to settle for 17th.
Matthew Hillier won two races with Adam Jones and Gavin Mason winning the other two. This, with good back-up from the Boys, ensured that we won with ease.
Intermediate Boy Gavin Mason continued his series of fine runs over the country by placing 63rd to be 3rd scorer for Surrey, helping them get to 9th of the 43 counties taking part.
Adam Jones and Gavin Mason decided it was time for us to see their new french plaited hairstyles and although they were not particularly aerodynamic, they did look nice.
Present at this meeting were two of our athletes who had won at the English Schools Championships - James Hilston who had won the Junior Boys 400m and Gavin Mason who won the Intermediate boys 800m.

Stephen Whorlow has developed quite a large group of very enthusiastic boys and girls down there so John and Leo Coy our two captains Toby Earle and Gavin Mason and I went down to Kent for a good coaching session.
Gavin Mason, just over the 'flu', and Adam Jones led the team throughout with Toby Earle running a 'blinder', hitting that hill as if he was having his own personal battle with the elements.

He steadily picked up eight places and was followed by Gavin Mason, who took another six, but we were just that bit too far back to do any real damage now, even with Matt Hillier setting the day's 7th fastest time on the last leg.

…Common, Matt Hillier later said that the jarring on his legs made him feel as if he had 'shin-splints' up to his waist. Gavin Mason headed the field after the loop, with Matt and Adam Jones in tow not far behind. Already we looked set for another team win.…
♦ Another who competes in two sporting spheres is Gavin Mason. Gavin competes regularly as a swimmer and a couple of months ago he retained his club breast-stroke championship.

Gavin Mason took the under-17 800 metres, drawing to within striking distance of John Gladwin's Club record, while James Hilston set new under-15 figures for the 400 metres, breaking a record that has stood for 32 years.
Above: Ranked at number 2 under 17 in the country over 800 metres, Gavin Mason prepares for a leg in a McDonalds YA League 4x400m.

Pride of place goes to our two champions James Hilston and Gavin Mason. James coolly took 2nd place in his opening round of the Junior 400m, setting a personal best, and the semi also saw him giving little away to the opposition with a 3rd place in yet another best.

Gavin Mason's winning 800m run showed that he has great things in store this summer and two others who won county titles for the first time were Jessica Dash, looking really confident over the hurdles, and Roger Alsop who controlled the 10k as if he's been running them for years.

But pride of place must go to 16 year-old Gavin Mason who was drafted into the 'B' 800 as a last minute replacement. Expected to gain only a single point he ignored the reputations of the opposition, raced well and was rewarded with an excellent pb and 4 points.
The Under 17s are missing Matt Hillier in the County Champs but have a scoring four right at the front. Left to right are Gavin Mason (9), Toby Earle (1), Scott Walsh, and Adam Jones (6)

It was a slightly worrying sight for Gavin Mason, waiting to make his début in this event in the 'B' race as Rob limped home for the point. Marlon Dickson was delighted with his 100 metres pb of 11.8 to equal Ludwig Nunoo's Club Record and he also scored heavily in the 200m and long jump.

This time, when Robert Milner ran the 400m hurdles he did not fall, thus he returned to his winning form, and Gavin Mason won the B race. After equalling the U13 1500m Club Record at the last meeting, Olivier Bazin broke it by nearly two seconds, gaining victory in the process.
The senior boys' 800 saw last year's leading inters Toby Dolman (Crawley AC and now 2nd-claim Belgrave) and Gavin Mason matching strides again.

Right: Gavin Mason pauses between reps while Clive Shippen gets busy with the camera. When Gavin clocked 48.89 to place 7th in the British League 'A' 400 metres on 2nd July he further complicated a little statistical anomaly.
Darryl Maynard earned a Welsh vest in the subsequent Turkey match after doubling up while Youth Gavin Mason opened the season by equalling his 800 pb to the 1/100th sec.
We had no winners but the team had a very pleasing look of youth about it as our U20s and U17s, led by Ben Cascoe and Gavin Mason joined the old war-horses of the Southern League.

Captain Mike Bazire was everywhere "filling in" instead of concentrating on his favoured events and with wins from Gavin "Sunshine" Mason (would you believe it - he was the only one who managed to compete without getting a soaking), Aham Amadi, Neil Hammersley and Jamie Webb, we managed to avoid las…

Well done to Gavin Mason (17), Marcel Fok (20), John Dawson (20) and Ian Wells (don't ask) who ran a pb split of 49.1. We were just pipped by Haringey in the sprint relay - not surprising as they fielded Mensah, Jarrett, Callender and Wariso.
Gavin Mason cruised a very comfortable two laps to give us our only scoring track win and then showed the enthusiasm that our young team exudes by filling in as a triple jumper!
Michael Parper, Ben Williams and Gavin Mason got the baton to Frazer Hazlett in the lead but with the opposition queuing up to run him down.

Gavin Mason put a disappointing 800 metre performance in Cyprus behind him by racing to a pb by nearly two seconds. In Nicosia for the World Schools Games he had clocked 1:56.65 but did not progress to the final.

At Reigate in the Surrey Champs. we had three Belgrave runners in the first eight in the Senior Boys' race. Matt Hillier and Adam Jones gave South Surrey a great start but it was Gavin Mason's Central Surrey team that took the winners' trophy.

Sixteen year-old Marlon Dickson looked sharp and got the verdict in the closest of finishes in the 100m while for Ben Williams' and Gavin Mason's races our two track judges, aided by a helpful schoolboy who had turned up simply to watch, had things a little easier.

Middle-distance man Gavin Mason was also looking for records. Simon Weston immediately took up the running in the 800m but a full 500 metres from home it was Gavin striding to the front and going away with a powerful raking stride that did not falter for a second over the remainder of the race.
Gavin Mason was 3rd, just half a stride behind 2nd place in a personal record. We haven't included Tom's win in our medal haul but a couple of months later he signed up for the Bels.
4x400m Relay · 3:28.1 · Gavin Mason (52.1) · 1st, National Junior League Division 3 South A, Perivale · 23 Apr 1995
Another teenager who seems to be making the grade nicely is Gavin Mason. Always looking for a fast time Gavin has felt moved to take up the pace himself in nearly all his races this year.

Gavin Mason has been in the squad regularly now but match 4 gave him his first BAL win in the 'B' 800m. At last it was down to the pb zone for two-lap racer Gavin Mason. After a 1:54.8 in the heats on day one he came up against Braintree's Tom Lerwill who had posted a 1:51/48 800m/400m double a week earlier and was brimming with confidence.

Gavin Mason had spurned the U20M 800m event in an attempt to find a fast time with the seniors. Sadly everyone played into the hands of Haringey's Fairbrother who had far too much pace after a first lap dawdle.
At Sutton Arena it was Richard David's turn to notch up a sprint double while Gavin Mason returned to the team to collect top points in the 400m.
